itemListElement.name: How to write board minutes of meeting in India in 2026, with format and sample

mainEntity.name: What is the time limit for board minutes in India?

acceptedAnswer.text: SS-1 sets 15 days for draft minutes to reach directors and 7 days for their comments. Section 118 requires minutes to be prepared, signed and kept within 30 days. A certified copy of the signed minutes goes to directors within 15 days of signing.

mainEntity.name: Who signs board minutes of meeting?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rule 25(1)(d) of the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014 puts the last page in the hands of the chairperson of that meeting, or of the next one. General meeting minutes differ: the same chairperson signs within 30 days, or a director the board authorises if that chairperson dies or cannot act.

mainEntity.name: How long must board minutes be preserved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rule 25(1)(f) says board and committee minute books are preserved permanently, in the custody of the company secretary or a director the board authorises, at the registered office or wherever the board decides. SS-1 treats the supporting papers differently: notices and agenda notes are kept for 8 financial years.

mainEntity.name: Can board minutes be changed after signing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Signed minutes should not be altered. Any correction belongs in a later board meeting's minutes, approved and recorded there. The cost of editing instead is set out in Section 118(12): tampering with minutes can mean imprisonment up to 2 years, plus a fine of ₹25,000 to ₹1,00,000.

Board minutes are internal records, not public filings. Section 119 gives members an inspection right over general meeting minute books only, with a copy due within 7 working days of a request. Board minutes stay with directors, auditors and authorities, and some resolutions are still filed with the Registrar of Companies.

Yes. Under Section 120, records including minutes may be kept and inspected in electronic form in the prescribed manner, and SS-1 adds that electronic minutes carry a timestamp. Content, the 30-day timeline and the signatures stay the same as on paper.
